results.content: This resulted in a set of global indicators (of which some are listed in Table 3) tracked by the GWP (in addition to GEF and LDCF core indicators): Table 3: Some of the global indicators tracked by the GWP Ecological and Conservation Outcomes Enabling Conditions and System Strengthening • Stabilization or increase in populations of, and area occupied by, wildlife program sites • Reduced threats to the ecological integrity of wildlife habitats • Reduced threats to wildlife from poaching and illegal activities • Strengthened Integrated Landscape Management to address threats and improve connectivity • Increased HWC (Human-Wildlife Conﬂict) Strategies and site interventions deployed • Improve enforcement, judicial, and prosecutorial institutional capacity to combat wildlife crime • Strengthened institutional and technical capacity for protected area management • More inclusive governance and increased community engagement in the stewardship of wildlife habitats • Enhanced policy, legal, and regulatory frameworks to foster a wildlife-based economy • Strengthening the capacity of stakeholders to develop non-forest timber products and sustainable use activities • Diversiﬁed and resilient livelihoods to build community support for wildlife-based economy, coexistence, decreasing wildlife crime and illegal use of wildlife-based economy • Improved coordination among countries’ donors, and other key stakeholders engaged in the implementation of the GWP • Improved knowledge sharing on wildlife conservation 27 Learning and adapting The GWP results framework is evolving in GEF-8, because of experience during the previous two phases and in response to recommendations made by the IEO45.
